guard: a peer-authored record opens a run and republishes no body, while a self-authored one still emits its content in full
why: An event channel carries a different read ACL from the channel a peer message arrived on, so
re-emitting an injected mesh message's text there is a republication across an ACL boundary.
The claim is joined, so it gets a mutation per fact. 'No peer content is emitted' is satisfied
completely by a mapper that emits nothing at all, which is why A2 exists: it suppresses every
body and must redden the liveness arm while leaving the safety arm green. If one mutation
reddened both, the two arms would be one axis under two names.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite imports the mapper by relative source path (../src/agui-map.js) and
calls it directly. Its only other import is connector-core's event constructors, which no
mutation below touches, so a kill comes from the mapper and not from the vocabulary.

mutations.name: A1 attribute the turn but stop withholding the body
mutations.expectRed: a peer record's text does NOT appear anywhere on the wire
mutations.cell: a peer record's text does NOT appear anywhere on the wire
mutations.note: This is not hypothetical: it is exactly what the mapper did before the filter existed, measured at 240 bytes in and 240 bytes out on a real session.

mutations.name: A2 withhold every body, peer and human alike
mutations.expectRed: DECOY/LIVENESS — a self-authored record DOES still emit its content
mutations.cell: DECOY/LIVENESS — a self-authored record DOES still emit its content
mutations.note: The over-broad filter, which passes every safety cell in the file. Without a liveness arm this mutant survives and the suite goes green against a mapper that publishes no prose at all.
